content.title: Dash Crofts, Seals & Crofts Member and 'Summer Breeze' Singer, Dies at 87
content.text: Dash Crofts circa 1975. Credit : Michael Ochs Archives/Getty NEED TO KNOW Dash Crofts of Seals & Crofts has died at the age of 87News of his death was confirmed by Seals & Crofts' producer Louie Shelton, who called him his "brother," on Thursday, March 26Jim Seals of Seals & Crofts died in June 2022 at the age of 79 Darrell "Dash" Crofts, one half of Seals & Crofts, the '70s yacht-rock group behind "Summer Breeze," has died. He was 87. News of his death was confirmed by Seals & Crofts' producer Louie Shelton in a Facebook post on Thursday, March 26. A family member told TMZ that Crofts died from complications following heart surgery. "Sad to hear our dear brother and partner in music has passed away today," he began the caption. "Sending love and prayers to all his family and many fans. R.I.P. my brother.....Dash Crofts." Dash Crofts in Los Angeles in January 1980. Ron Galella/Ron Galella Collection via Getty Born in Cisco, Texas, Crofts began playing the piano at the age of 5 before taking up the drums by the time he turned 10. By high school, he played drums in a band, where he met Jim Seals, who was playing saxophone at the time. After high school, Crofts and Seals relocated to Southern California and became members of The Champs from 1958 to 1965. The duo began working together under the name Seals & Crofts in 1969 and by the '70s, they landed hits including "Summer Breeze" and "Diamond Girl." During a 1971 interview with Stereo Review, Crofts reflected on the band's sound moving in a breezier direction. “I think we’d be better off not even to classify it,” he said at the time. "Some people have called it religious music. It’s not actually religious music, though it is inspired by religion. But no particular musical group influenced us, and I think that’s one of the reasons that what is coming out is really us.” Related Stories Crofts noted that after he and Seals had "been in the hard rock scene for a long, long time," they wanted to make something different. "Playing [hard rock] gets to be pretty tough physically after a while. … It’s such a nice relief to just sit and play pretty stuff for a change," he ssaid. The group, who released more than a dozen albums, including their 1972 breakthrough fourth record Summer Breeze and Greatest Hits in 1975, also earned four gold albums go gold and two platinum ones. Dash Crofts and Jim Seals in April 1975. Michael Putland/Getty Throughout their career, Seals & Crofts earned two Grammy nominations from "Diamond Girl" and "We Will Never Pass This Way (Again)." In 1983, the pair went their separate ways before reuniting 1990s and in 2004, when they teamed up for their first album since 1980 with Traces. In 1998, Crofts released his first solo album, Today. Dash Crofts and Jim Seals in February 1989 in L.A. Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection via Getty Seals died in June 2022 at the age of 79. CBS News reported that the late musician died at his home outside of Nashville with his family by his side. At the time, his wife Ruby told The New York Times that Seals died of an undisclosed but "chronic ongoing illness." "We are forever inspired by his selfless life of service and his pure and kindly heart that touched all who crossed his path," his family told CBS in a statement. "We extend our gratitude for the outpouring of love and support we continue to receive from around the globe by those who have been touched by his life and music."
